entry.title: [HIGH] Plugin marketplace auto-update can block PreToolUse dispatch on Windows.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code VS Code extension 2.1.240-2.1.241 Windows repro found plugin marketplace auto-update work running synchronously inside the PreToolUse hook path for unrelated tool calls such as Edit. With multiple concurrent Claude Code sessions in one VS Code window, one session could hold a handle on the shared plugin cache while another tried to clone, remove, or replace the same marketplace directory. Windows then returned `EBUSY`, the updater retried, and the affected tool call and chat session appeared to hang for minutes with no visible plugin-update status. The report included logs showing slow PreToolUse hooks, plugin autoupdate `EBUSY` failures, repeated cache clones, and a webview input-lag sample of about 392 seconds before the user closed the stalled tab.

entry.title: [HIGH] Auto mode can approve unsandboxed Bash retries without seeing the sandbox override.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 macOS repro found that an auto-mode Bash retry with `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` could write outside the sandbox without showing the user a permission prompt. The reporter traced the shipped binary path where Bash permission checking recognizes a sandbox-override ask, but auto mode falls through to the classifier and the classifier input contains only the shell command, not the sandbox-disable flag. In the observed transcript the unsandboxed write was summarized as file reading, and the assistant then told the user the override had gone through the permission gate even though the user never had a chance to answer.

entry.title: [HIGH] Assistant output can append foreign page content to a live response.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.237 macOS VS Code extension session appended about 15 KB of unrelated third-party web page UI text into an in-flight assistant message. The transcript showed the same API request ID as the legitimate reply, with the foreign content arriving about 81 seconds after the real final sentence and streaming until the user interrupted it. The reporter ruled out local proxy tooling and found the foreign string only in the affected session transcript, making the incident distinct from ordinary hallucinated wording or user-pasted content. Because the injected block was stored as assistant output, later turns could treat unrelated external text as trusted conversation history.

entry.title: [HIGH] Custom auto-mode deny rules can be loaded but inert.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.240 Fedora repro found that user-level `autoMode.hard_deny` and `autoMode.soft_deny` entries could be parsed, merged with `$defaults`, and displayed by `claude auto-mode config` while still failing to affect classifier behavior. Matched scratch-HOME trials differed only by the custom deny rule, but both allowed the forbidden `rm victim.txt` action to delete the target file. The reporter also observed real custom hard-deny floors failing to block off-allowlist `git push` attempts in interactive sessions, while custom `autoMode.allow` entries did appear to change behavior. This makes `auto-mode config` output insufficient proof that a user-authored deny floor is actually enforced.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows CoworkVMService can loop before configuring the isolated workspace.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 11 Claude Desktop Cowork setup could not start the isolated Linux workspace used by `device_bash`: every shell attempt returned `Workspace unavailable`, while file-based bridge tools still worked. `CoworkVMService` started, initialized HCS and HCN, opened its named pipe server, and logged signature-verification setup, but then only logged repeated `[Server] Client connected` lines for hours. It never logged a configure call, VM creation attempt, timeout, or explanatory error, and the behavior persisted after enabling Hyper-V, confirming Windows Hypervisor Platform, deleting the service, clearing `C:\ProgramData\Claude`, reinstalling, and rebooting.

entry.title: [HIGH] Always Allow for shell redirects can write rules that never satisfy the blocked gate.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 repro found that when a Bash command is blocked because shell output redirection writes outside the session working directory, the permission prompt can still offer an `Always Allow` option that persists Bash and Read rules. Those rules do not cover the filesystem write gate that actually blocked the redirect, so the byte-identical command prompts again one tool call later and keeps proposing the same ineffective persistent grant. Repeated approvals accumulate allow entries while never terminating the prompt loop.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Scheduled-task runs can leak completed session process pairs.
entry.summary: A reported macOS Claude Code 2.1.237 Desktop scheduled-task setup completed each task normally, wrote an `end_turn` transcript, then left both the `Contents/Helpers/disclaimer` parent and `claude` child process alive indefinitely. The reporter found 33 leaked sessions across 8 scheduled tasks, including a 21-second job still resident 29 hours later, with each child holding API connections and about 220 MB. On a host with one hourly task plus several daily tasks, the accumulated leak was estimated around 16 GB of resident memory per day.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Idle Claude Code sessions can burn CPU through timer-triggered garbage collection.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.240 Linux native session continued using measurable CPU while parked at the input prompt with no active turn. Controlled 30-second samples showed a pristine config using about 0.3-0.8% CPU and a typical config with plugins, hooks, one MCP server, and CLAUDE.md using about 1.46% CPU; longer production sessions measured about 1.4-5% while idle. The reporter traced the idle cost to short timers waking the event loop roughly 20-26 times per second in a typical config, about one Eden garbage collection per second, and repeated wakeups of JavaScriptCore helper threads and mimalloc cleanup work even when the terminal output did not change.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows VS Code extension file watching can pin one CPU core.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.240 VS Code extension setup on Windows 11 repeatedly left an extension host pinned at 95-100% of one performance core for hours while Claude Code's own extension log showed only idle heartbeats. The reporter sampled the spinning process at about 245,000 other I/O operations per second with essentially zero reads, matching a native watched-directory busy-loop rather than ordinary JavaScript or scan work. Duplicate watch paths through NTFS junctions into shared Claude config trees and bulk skill rewrites appeared to amplify the problem, but one spin latched about 35 minutes after the last file change and persisted until the extension host was killed.

entry.title: [HIGH] Desktop Cowork can advertise MCP elicitation without rendering UI.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop Cowork session on macOS used an embedded claude-code runtime that declared the MCP `elicitation` capability for the session handling `tools/call`, while a sibling `Anthropic/ClaudeAI` session to the same server did not. When the MCP server sent `elicitation/create`, the embedded client accepted the request but rendered no form in the Desktop UI, returned no display error, and only resolved the elicitation as cancelled after the originating tool call hit the client's 60-second timeout. Servers therefore cannot distinguish a user reading a displayed approval form from a hidden form that will never appear, even though the capability bit steers them onto the elicitation path.

entry.title: [HIGH] Subagents can inherit stale CLAUDE.md and memory snapshots.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.237 Linux session found that Agent-tool subagents received the CLAUDE.md and memory content captured when the parent session started, not the files as they existed when the subagent was spawned. In the report, a parent session started at 12:31 and dispatched a subagent at 21:10, so the subagent saw context that was 8h39m old. A memory file deleted from disk after parent startup still appeared in the child context, while memory files written later were absent. Because the stale instructions were not marked stale, the subagent could confidently act on a superseded rule that no longer existed on disk.

entry.title: [HIGH] Nested repository hooks are not loaded from parent-root sessions.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code multi-repo workflow keeps dependent checkouts inside a parent workspace and starts the session at the parent root. When tool calls operate inside a nested repository, that nested repo's `.claude/settings.json` hooks are not discovered or loaded, and directories added with `--add-dir` are documented as file-access grants rather than settings or hook roots. This means a child checkout can carry project-specific PreToolUse, lint, test, protected-path, or custody hooks that never fire while the parent session edits it. Parent hooks can still fire in the child cwd, so users may see hook activity while the child repo's own guardrails remain absent. The reporter explicitly notes that arbitrary nested hook auto-loading would be unsafe without a separate trust decision, making the practical gap a missing trust-gated way to opt into nested hook roots.

entry.title: [HIGH] Bash deny patterns can be bypassed by git flag prefixes.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code Windows Git Bash session with `permissions.defaultMode: "acceptEdits"` found that destructive Git deny rules such as `Bash(git checkout -- *)`, `Bash(git restore *)`, `Bash(git reset --hard *)`, and `Bash(git branch -D *)` matched the bare command form but were bypassed when a flag appeared before the subcommand, for example `git -C <repo> checkout -- <file>`. The prefixed command matched neither the user's allow nor deny pattern and still executed without a confirmation prompt, silently discarding an uncommitted file change in the repro. This makes raw command-prefix matching unsafe for destructive Bash policies because common git flags such as `-C`, `-c`, `--git-dir`, or `--work-tree` can move the dangerous verb away from the literal start of the command.

entry.title: [HIGH] Remote Control spawned sessions can ignore the requested permission mode.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.240 macOS Remote Control setup accepted `claude remote-control --permission-mode bypassPermissions` and propagated that flag onto spawned `sdk-cli` process arguments, but every spawned web or mobile-driven session still recorded and behaved as `auto`. Setting `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"` in user settings did not fix the Remote Control path, even though a direct local print session honored it. The same report found that messages from a more-permissive local session to the auto-mode Remote Control session were held for recipient approval, but no prompt appeared in the web/mobile app, host terminal, or subprocess UI, so the hold expired without a reachable approval surface.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Plan approval can authorize model-authored commands.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code plan-mode session treated approval of a model-authored plan as authority to run shell commands that appeared in the plan's verification section, even though the human had approved file edits but had not separately approved a build. The reporter's transcript extraction found two assistant-issued Bash calls containing the build command and zero human-typed turns containing that command before execution. The risky boundary is provenance: a command written by the model into an approved plan can be read back as part of the approved artifact, making plan approval look like per-command execution consent.

entry.title: [HIGH] Desktop hook failures can lose their diagnostics.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code desktop setup with relative project hook commands found that hook launch failures were invisible in the desktop UI and recorded only as `hook_non_blocking_error` transcript attachments with empty `content`. The reporter correlated more than 72,000 such records across months of sessions and found no errno, resolved path, exit status, stderr, or user-visible notice, even though guardrail hooks such as PreToolUse Edit and Bash groups were not running during cwd drift windows. This makes a failed policy hook look like normal operation unless users audit transcript internals or external hook logs.

entry.title: [HIGH] AskUserQuestion auto-results can look like human approval.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code subagent workflow found that `AskUserQuestion` returned the same success-shaped text whether a real human selected an option or the answer was produced automatically without any user seeing the prompt. In the reported case, isolated subagents asked approval questions for implementation and deletion decisions and received the recommended option as selected, but the parent user was never shown the questions. Agents that treat the tool result as a human approval gate can therefore proceed with consequential work from an auto-returned answer that has no visible provenance marker.

entry.title: [HIGH] Background bridge sessions can persistently disable project MCP servers.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code macOS background job launched through the claude.ai/code bridge wrote the project's `.mcp.json` server names into both `enabledMcpjsonServers` and `disabledMcpjsonServers` in `.claude/settings.local.json` at job startup. Because the disabled list wins and the file persists, previously approved project HTTP MCP servers stayed disabled for later interactive sessions too. The reporter found no transcript write to the settings file, which points to a harness startup mutation leaking a non-interactive launch limitation into durable project configuration.

entry.title: [HIGH] Auto Mode can bypass explicit Bash deny rules.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.239 macOS setup found that an explicit `permissions.deny` rule such as `Bash(curl *)` was enforced when the same session was switched to manual mode, but the identical `curl https://example.com` Bash command executed successfully while Auto Mode was active. The reporter reproduced the behavior in both a standalone CLI install and Claude Desktop's bundled Claude Code with the same settings excerpt, making the risk a mode-dependent gap rather than a missing rule. Users who treat static deny rules as a hard network-egress boundary can therefore get a silent allow when the auto-mode classifier considers a denied command benign.

entry.title: [HIGH] Print-mode read audits can finish with zero output.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.235 macOS print-mode repro found that `claude -p --no-session-persistence --permission-mode dontAsk --tools Read --output-format text` could complete a multi-file read-only audit with no stdout, no stderr, and a zero-byte redirected output file. Simple controls still worked: a tools-disabled PONG prompt and a one-file Read followed by PONG both returned output. The failure therefore leaves automation unable to distinguish a completed but lost audit report from a valid empty result unless the wrapper checks for content.
